author: DoIPutNameHere
quote: Wolverine is a major disappointment that struggles to live up to the potential of its character. The combat (while initially satisfying) becomes repetitive because many encounters boil down to repeatedly using the same claw attacks, dodges, and takedowns against groups of enemies without enough variety to keep fights interesting enough. The pacing also hurts the experience with story-heavy sections sometimes slowing the momentum between action sequences and making the overall campaign feel uneven. Even Wolverine's healing ability (which should be a defining part of his gameplay) can make encounters feel less tense because damage often becomes something the player can simply recover from rather than manage. The game's environments also feel more restrictive to the point of inducing claustrophobia. Most disappointing is the story, which introduces potentially interesting characters and conflicts but doesn't consistently give them enough development to make their emotional moments land. There are flashes of impressive visuals and brutal action, but those moments aren't enough to overcome the repetitive gameplay, uneven pacing, and missed potential.

author: DoIPutNameHere
quote:
I tried my hardest to get into this game and have played since the beta. Unfortunately many of the imperfections that prevented me from enjoying this has. I genuinely don't understand how this game left Early Access and called itself version 1.0. Underneath the decent looking trailers and creature designs is a repetitive survival game that never truly evolves beyond its first few hours. The entire gameplay loop becomes wildly predictable too. You just gather resources, craft better gear, catch another Pal, repeat. After dozens of hours it just feels like you're doing the same tasks in slightly different environments and that's it. The "open world" is enormous but much of it is filled with empty stretches that offer little reason to explore beyond checking another icon off the map.

Combat is another major disappointment to me. Guns lack impact, melee feels crazy stiff, enemy AI rarely presents any interesting challenges, and boss fights often boil down to dodging while your Pal does most of the work which lacks proper engagement. There's also very little strategy or mechanical depth compared to other action RPGs or survival games. Base building and automation should've been the game's strongest features, but instead they're a constant source of frustration. Pals still get stuck, ignore assigned jobs, prioritize random tasks or stop working altogether which can be very annoying. Managing your base often feels like fighting the AI instead of building something efficient... Even the creature collecting starts to lose its appeal surprisingly fast. While a handful of Pals look creative, too many serve nearly identical gameplay purposes making new captures feel more like checklist items than exciting discoveries. Technically speaking the game still feels very rough. Performance can be inconsistent, bugs still pop up far too often for a "finished" release, and the overall level of polish simply isn't where a full release should be at all. 

The biggest problem is that Palworld never decides what it wants to excel at. It borrows ideas from monster collecting, survival crafting, automation, base management, exploration, and action combat but never truly masters any of them. Instead of becoming greater than the sum of its parts, it ends up feeling like a collection of half-developed systems. By the end of my time playing, I wasn't too excited to unlock the next area or catch another Pal, I was simply waiting for the game to give me a reason to keep playing... that reason never came.

A promising concept buried beneath repetitive design, frustrating systems, and a lack of meaningful depth. Unless you're already a huge fan of the formula, it's difficult to recommend.

author: DoIPutNameHere
quote: Game sounds promising on paper, but it just didn't click for me. It looks impressive in trailers, and there are definitely moments where the world feels alive, but a lot of the time it felt uneven with weird pacing and game design choices. Some areas got way more attention than others. The combat started off fun, but after a few hours it got a little bit repetitive, and the controls feel kinda awkward especially in bigger fights. I also had a hard time getting into the story. It's not bad, but it's pretty forgettable and I never felt invested in what was going on or who the characters were. Overall I don't think it's terrible or anything, but it feels like this game needed way more time to be fully polished before release. I know the devs have been patching it which have been welcomed, but it should have launched in this state. I wouldn't say it's worth the price right now unless you're really into this type of game. I'd also recommend waiting until the end of the year until the devs continue polishing to the state it should have released in.
